practices.practice: Do not commit connection strings or keys; read the cluster URI from environment variables (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secret store (Key Vault) and provide an .env.example with placeholders only.
practices.prior_belief: Never commit the connection string or primary keys to source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any credentials) from environment variables or a secret store (Azure Key Vault) and provide an .env.example with placeholders only.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Mongoose connection best practices

practices.practice: Reuse a single MongoDB/Mongoose connection pool (singleton MongoClient) and set sensible pool/timeouts (maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) rather than opening per-request connections.
practices.prior_belief: Configure Mongoose/Mongo driver connection pooling and set sensible timeouts: use unifiedTopology: true, useNewUrlParser: true, maxPoolSize (e.g., 50), serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS to avoid hung connections on cloud clusters.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB MongoDB connection pooling Mongoose

practices.practice: Treat driver-level retryable-writes cautiously for Azure DocumentDB (examples keep retryWrites=false); do not rely on automatic retries for non-idempotent operations and plan application-level idempotency/deduplication instead.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB retryWrites guidance

practices.practice: Use MongoDB update operators like $set with dotted paths to merge into nested subdocuments instead of replacing entire documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use update operators ($set, $setOnInsert, $inc) and dot notation to merge source-specific nested sub-documents instead of replacing full documents (e.g., $set: { 'sources.crm': mergedFields }).
practices.source_name: Updating data in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB updateOne $set dot notation

practices.practice: Perform idempotent upserts by using a stable identifier (e.g., _id or a unique customerId) with updateOne/replaceOne and upsert:true so repeated events merge safely.
practices.prior_belief: Use a stable customerId as the document _id (or as the partition key + unique id) and perform upserts by _id to ensure idempotent merges: db.collection.updateOne({_id: customerId}, {$set: {...}}, {upsert: true}).
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB upsert examples updateOne upsert

practices.practice: Create indexes for queryable fields ahead of time (migration scripts/controlled deployment) rather than generating many indexes ad-hoc at runtime to avoid high write cost and index build overhead.
practices.prior_belief: Create an index on customerId (or _id) and any frequently queried nested attributes (e.g., sources.crm.email) ahead of time via migration scripts rather than creating indexes ad-hoc at runtime.
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB indexing best practices create indexes after bulk load

practices.practice: Create vector indexes (and other heavy indexes) with the cluster management tools or migration scripts and verify them with cluster/portal tools rather than creating them on every app startup.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes and any vector index using the cluster's management tools or migration scripts (not on every app start); verify index creation and query plans with the cluster's tools (MCP/portal) before running production traffic.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use vector search with Node.js in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index creation guidance

practices.practice: Choose a shard/partition key with high cardinality and even distribution that aligns with dominant query patterns (a stable customerId can be a good choice if each customer's data fits in a logical partition).
practices.prior_belief: Choose the partition key to be customerId (or another high-cardinality stable id) so each customer profile is co-located in one partition and single-document operations avoid cross-partition costs.
practices.source_name: Sharding for horizontal scalability in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB shard key partitioning best practices

practices.practice: When you shard a collection, ensure the shard key is indexed and prefer hashed or composite keys to avoid hot partitions; resharding is supported online but plan it carefully because changing shard keys is expensive.
practices.source_name: Sharding for horizontal scalability in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB how to shard a collection

practices.practice: For vector search, store vectors as numeric arrays and create a vector index with the correct dimensions/metric before querying; choose IVF/HNSW/DiskANN based on dataset size (DiskANN and M30+ for large indexes) and tune index parameters (numLists, efSearch, lBuild, lSearch) to balance recall and latency.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search: store normalized embedding arrays in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding.vector) with a consistent fixed dimension and create the cluster's vector index (HNSW/IVF) with matching dimension and metric before running similarity queries.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index algorithm guidance DiskANN HNSW IVF dimensions

practices.practice: Honor throttling signals (HTTP 429) from Azure services: respect Retry-After headers when present and otherwise use bounded exponential backoff with jitter; use circuit breakers and avoid retry storms/enqueuing retries that block threads.
practices.prior_belief: Handle rate limiting (HTTP 429 / RU throttling) and transient network errors by implementing exponential backoff and respecting Retry-After headers; avoid tight retry loops that amplify load.
practices.source_name: Design throttling to improve resilience
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB throttling 429 Retry-After best practices

practices.practice: Monitor RU/request-charge and query costs: collect diagnostic logs to Log Analytics or storage, use getLastRequestStatistics for query charges, and instrument the app to log requestCharge so you can detect and tune expensive operations.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/s consumption, request charge per query, index usage and latency with Azure Monitor/metrics and instrument the app to log requestCharge to detect expensive operations and tune indexes or queries accordingly.
practices.source_name: Monitor Azure DocumentDB diagnostics logs with Azure Monitor
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB monitor diagnostics requestCharge getLastRequestStatistics

practices.practice: Avoid indexing every field or large frequently-updated arrays; plan indexes only for fields used in filters/sorts and avoid wildcard or broad indexing unless query patterns justify the write-cost increase.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid indexing very large or frequently-updated sub-doc arrays; instead, index only the fields used in filters/sorts. Remove wildcard indexing on entire documents unless necessary to reduce RU costs.
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB avoid wildcard indexing cost

practices.practice: Provision throughput sized to expected traffic and consider autoscale for variable workloads rather than manual overprovisioning.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput according to expected traffic and consider autoscale or database-level (shared) throughput for dev/test; ensure RU provisioning matches the seed/load script to avoid 429s during seeding.
practices.source_name: How to choose between standard (manual) and autoscale provisioned throughput
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB autoscale vs manual throughput guidance

practices.practice: Enforce TLS for all client connections and restrict network access with firewall rules and Private Link; prefer Microsoft Entra ID and least-privilege database users over using admin keys for runtime applications.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL for all connections and enable firewall/VNet restrictions, IP allowlists and least-privilege database users; do not use admin keys for application runtime if role-based access or scoped secondary users are available.
practices.source_name: Frequently asked questions about Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB security TLS Private Link Entra ID guidance

practices.practice: Keep single-document upserts/updates for best performance; use multi-document transactions only when needed and only where the service supports them (multi-document transactions are supported within a single nonsharded collection).
practices.prior_belief: Keep upsert operations as single-document updates (no multi-document transactions) for performance; if you must perform multi-document atomic changes, consider transactions but only when supported and necessary.
practices.source_name: Use Multi-document transactions in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB transactions supported scope single nonsharded collection

practices.practice: Use optimistic concurrency control (ETag / If-Match or a lastModified field) to detect concurrent writes and avoid lost updates where appropriate.
practices.prior_belief: Use optimistic concurrency where appropriate: read _etag (Cosmos) or check a lastModified field to detect concurrent writes and avoid lost updates when multiple sources update the same profile concurrently.
practices.source_name: Transactions and optimistic concurrency control
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB optimistic concurrency _etag If-Match guidance

practices.practice: Run integration/seed scripts and tests against a dedicated development database name that is configurable (env var) and clean up test data after runs to avoid accidental changes to production databases.
practices.prior_belief: Write integration/seed scripts and tests to target a dedicated database name (sample_customer_360_01 here) and to clean up test data after runs; make DB name configurable via env var to avoid accidental cross-database changes.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB quickstart use dedicated development database and cleanup

practices.practice: Enforce DB-side uniqueness when needed: on the Mongo API create unique indexes for identity fields; on other APIs use the platform's unique-key policy where available.
practices.prior_belief: Create collection/container-level unique constraints for customer identity if you need DB-enforced uniqueness (Cosmos uses uniqueKey policy; Mongo API supports unique indexes) rather than relying on application logic alone.
practices.source_name: MongoDB Query Language (MQL) compatibility in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB unique index support documentation

practices.practice: Avoid documents that exceed the MongoDB/DocumentDB maximum document size (16 MB for Mongo-compatible documents) and move large blobs to external storage when needed.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid large documents that exceed the service document size limits (e.g., 2MB/16MB depending on API); keep customer profile documents reasonably small or split rarely-used large blobs into separate storage.
practices.source_name: Compare Azure DocumentDB to MongoDB Atlas
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB document size limit 16-MB

practices.practice: Create indexes that support your sorts (e.g., lastUpdated) and prefer cursor/range-based pagination (filter by lastSeen / lastUpdated > value) over skip/limit for large collections to reduce RU consumption.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes for sorting queries you run (e.g., lastUpdated) and prefer range-based pagination (filter by lastUpdated > lastSeen) over skip/limit for large collections to reduce RU cost.
practices.source_name: Manage indexing in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB indexing for sort and pagination guidance

practices.practice: Validate schemas in the application layer (Mongoose schemas/validators) and optionally enable server-side JSON Schema validation ($jsonSchema) where supported; keep schema migrations scripted and repeatable.
practices.prior_belief: Perform schema validation in the application layer (Mongoose schemas/validators) and optionally enable server-side validation where supported to avoid corrupt/invalid profiles; keep schema migrations scripted and repeatable.
